title: [C14T2] - Export earnings
prompt: The chart shows export values of one country by category for 2015-2016. The table shows percentage changes between these years. Summarise the main features and make comparisons.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The bar chart illustrates the export earnings of a country across five product categories in 2015 and 2016, while the accompanying table presents the percentage changes in each category during this period.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, export revenues increased in four out of five categories between 2015 and 2016, with only gems and jewellery experiencing a decline. Additionally, petroleum products consistently generated the highest earnings, while textiles recorded the most significant growth rate at over 15%.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Looking at the absolute values, petroleum products dominated export earnings in both years, generating approximately 60 billion dollars in 2015 and rising to roughly 62 billion in 2016. Engineered goods ranked second, earning around 57 billion dollars in 2015 and increasing to about 60 billion the following year. Gems and jewellery started at approximately 42 billion dollars in 2015 but declined to around 39 billion in 2016. The remaining categories, agricultural products and textiles, showed lower earnings, with agricultural products maintaining steady figures of about 30 billion dollars in both years, while textiles rose from 25 billion to approximately 31 billion dollars.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Regarding the percentage changes shown in the table, textiles experienced the most dramatic growth at 15.24%, followed by engineered goods with an 8.5% increase. Petroleum products recorded a modest rise of 3%, while agricultural products showed minimal growth of just 0.81%. Conversely, gems and jewellery was the only sector to contract, declining by 5.18% over the period.
